items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: playing for I guess it was a 1923 film by Harold Lloyd called “The Freshman.”

ctx.x: I have done that. I’m much too young to have played that era, but since then I have occasionally done it. Not too long ago I played on a Mighty Wurlitzer organ in Seattle at the Paramount Theater, playing for I guess it was a 1923 film by Harold Lloyd called “The Freshman.” That’s hard work. That’s an hour and ten minutes, in that case, of playing and trying to know what you’re going to do, and working the controls of the
organ and also craning your head up like that trying to watch the film at the same time. And people who did it in those days would do like four, five or six of those a day, forever.
